threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success metrics, and 30-day onboarding journey map.

messages.text: Kicking off the Launch of Company-Wide Hybrid Onboarding Program project_title in this channel. Goal: have a standardized 30-day hybrid onboarding ready for pilot within 21 days, covering both remote and on-site hires and staying within the 8-hour training cap in week one. I will own T1 and T11 from the backlog and partner closely with 54023 on T2. For scope, I suggest we focus on: 1) a 30-day journey map, 2) core training content and facilitator support, 3) manager and HR assistant toolkits, and 4) a simple evaluation and reporting framework. Please react or comment if you see anything missing before we lock this as our working scope under D1.

This scope works for me. On T2, I can draft the 30-day journey map so that it respects the 8-hour cap in week one and the 2-hour weekly limit for managers. I will structure it around mandatory vs optional modules to reduce overload, and we can later plug in the survey touchpoints from T11. Before I start, can we confirm whether compliance topics should all sit in week one, or can we stagger some of them into week two without creating risk?

From a policy standpoint, we need core compliance items covered before new hires start working independently, but not everything has to be in the first few days. I suggest we keep code of conduct, health and safety basics, and data protection in week one, and move deeper policy details to week two as long as they are clearly marked as mandatory. We can document this split in A1 once T2 is drafted.

On scope, I would add one explicit point: manager and buddy engagement. We have a risk that managers revert to old habits, so I would like the manager toolkit and the reporting from T11 to include a light way to see if managers are completing their part. Maybe a simple field in the tracking sheet later, but at least a metric in the success framework.

From the HR assistant side, I just want to confirm that the admin checklist and tracking process are also in scope. I see T5 and T7 in the backlog, and I can start drafting the admin checklist, but I will need guidance on how detailed the tracking needs to be so it does not become too heavy for each intake.

Yes, T5 and T7 are definitely in scope, and they will connect later with the success metrics in T11. For now, keep the admin checklist focused on contracts, payroll setup, system access, and mandatory forms. We will keep the tracking process itself simple, probably a shared sheet, so that we do not add too much admin work.

Thanks, that split helps. I will reflect it in the first version of A1. Plan: 1) draft the 30-day journey map for T2 with clear tags for compliance vs role-specific vs culture modules, 2) mark which items are live vs self-paced, and 3) leave placeholders for the day 7 and day 30 surveys that will come from T11. I can share a draft for review by tomorrow.

On success metrics for T11, I propose we track at least: 1) completion rate of mandatory modules within 30 days, 2) satisfaction scores from new hires and managers at day 7 and day 30, and 3) time to basic productivity, which we can approximate via manager feedback. We can refine the exact questions later when we design the surveys, but I want to confirm that these three areas match expectations before I draft the framework.

Those three areas make sense to me. For time to basic productivity, maybe we can keep it simple and ask managers at day 30 whether the new hire can perform core tasks with minimal supervision. That way we do not need extra systems. We can capture that in the survey templates later.

Agree with the three metrics. I would just add that we should watch for information overload in week one. Maybe we can include one or two questions in the day 7 survey about pacing and clarity, and then use that feedback to adjust A1 after the pilot.

Once you share the draft of A1, could you highlight where HR assistants are expected to step in? It will help me later when I work on T5 and T7 so that the admin steps line up with the journey map and we do not miss any touchpoints.
Yes, I will add a lane in A1 for HR assistants so that your steps are visible across the 30 days. That should make it easier to plug in T5 and T7 later without rework.

I will start T1 today and run quick interviews with 5 to 7 managers to validate the main onboarding gaps and must-have topics. The findings will help us stress-test the scope and the first draft of A1. I will share a short summary note in this thread once done so we can adjust before we call the scope final under D1.

Update on T1: I have completed 5 manager interviews. Main themes: 1) inconsistent coverage of policies, 2) lack of clarity on who owns which step, and 3) too much content in the first week. This confirms that our focus on a clear 30-day journey map, manager toolkit, and simple metrics is on the right track. Unless anyone objects, I suggest we confirm the scope as described in M1 plus the explicit manager engagement point from M4 and move ahead under D1.

No objections from me. The scope feels balanced and aligned with what managers raised in T1. Once A1 is drafted, I can help review it from a policy and clarity angle before we sign off on it under D2.

I have uploaded the first draft of A1 for T2. It includes: 1) a day-by-day outline for the first 30 days, 2) clear tags for mandatory vs optional modules, 3) separate lanes for managers, buddies, HR assistants, and new hires, and 4) placeholders for the day 7 and day 30 surveys from T11. Please review and drop comments today so we can iterate once and then aim to approve the journey map under D2.

I have reviewed A1. The split between week one and week two compliance topics looks safe, and the total time in week one stays within the 8-hour cap. I added a small comment on clarifying data protection wording, but otherwise I am comfortable. From my side, we can move to approve A1 under D2 once others have had a quick look.

I checked A1 as well. The HR assistant lane is clear for contracts, payroll, and system access. I did not see anything that conflicts with how we currently set people up, so I am fine with this version.

Thanks all for the quick reviews. Given the feedback from 472663 and 84941 and the alignment with T1 findings, I propose we formally approve the 30-Day Hybrid Onboarding Journey Map A1 as the baseline for this project under D2. Any further tweaks can be handled as minor updates, but the structure and scope are now fixed.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize core training content and facilitator guide for live sessions.

messages.text: I have uploaded the first draft of the Core Onboarding Training Deck A2 for T3, based on the approved journey map A1. It covers company overview, values, HR policies, and code of conduct, and I have kept the total live delivery time to 90 minutes so we stay within the 2-hour weekly limit for managers. I also started a skeleton for the facilitator guide for T8, but it still needs more detail. Please review the deck content first so we can move toward sign-off under D3.

Thanks for sharing. I will review A2 today with a focus on policy accuracy and alignment with A1. One question upfront: do you see the live session as a single 90-minute block, or would it be better to split into two shorter sessions to reduce fatigue? This will influence what we confirm later under D4 for standard format and duration.

I did a first pass on A2. Content-wise, the policy sections look broadly correct, but I left comments on a few items that need updated wording to match our latest HR policies. Once those are adjusted, I am comfortable from a compliance angle. For the format, I lean toward two shorter live sessions, especially for remote hires, but I am open to your view as the trainer.

I like the structure of A2. The flow from company story to values to policies feels natural. I added a suggestion to include one short reflection question after the values section to make it more engaging. No blockers from my side, just minor tweaks.

I went through A2 mainly to see where HR assistants might be mentioned. I noticed the slide on admin support and system access. Could we add a brief note there about where new hires can find the admin checklist once T5 is ready, so they know what to expect from us?

Good point on format. My proposal for D4 is: two live sessions of 45 minutes each, both delivered in the first week. Session one: company overview and values. Session two: HR policies and code of conduct. That keeps each block manageable for remote and on-site hires and still fits within the 2-hour weekly limit for managers. I will adjust A2 and the T8 facilitator guide draft to reflect this split.

Thanks for the compliance comments on A2. I will update the policy wording today and flag any items where I am unsure so you can double-check. Once those edits are in, could you confirm in this thread that the deck is compliant so we can move toward sign-off under D3?

Good catch. I will add a note in the admin support slide pointing to the HR Assistant Onboarding Admin Checklist A4 once it is finalized from T5. That way new hires know what is handled behind the scenes and where to look if they have questions.

On T8, I have now fleshed out the facilitator guide draft A6. It includes timing for each slide, key messages, and interaction tips for both in-person and virtual delivery. I also added notes on how to handle common questions that might overlap with the FAQ work later. Please review A6 alongside A2 so we can refine both together.

I like the proposal of two 45-minute sessions. It gives us a clear standard to communicate to managers and fits the constraints. Unless anyone sees a strong reason not to, I suggest we adopt that as our standard format and duration for live onboarding sessions under D4.

I have rechecked A2 after your edits. The policy wording now matches our current HR documents, and the mandatory elements are clearly marked. From a compliance perspective, I am comfortable approving this version of the deck for use in the pilot.

I reviewed A6. The interaction tips are practical, especially the prompts for remote participants. I added one suggestion to include a short check-in question at the start of each session to build rapport. Otherwise, it looks ready for the pilot from my side.

I skimmed A6 mainly to see if there are any points where HR assistants need to be present. It looks like we are not required in the live sessions, which is fine, but if you want us to join the first pilot run to help with questions in chat, I can try to make time.

Given the agreement on two 45-minute sessions and the compliance green light on A2 from 472663, I suggest we formally sign off the Core Onboarding Training Deck under D3. A2 is now our standard deck for the pilot, and A6 is our reference facilitator guide for live delivery.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on manager toolkit, HR admin checklist, and tracking process.

messages.text: I have posted a draft of the Manager Onboarding Toolkit and Checklist A3 for T4. It includes a manager checklist, a sample 1:1 agenda, and a 30-day plan template aligned with A1. 54023, I would appreciate your review for clarity and flow. 84941, once we align on the manager side, we should connect it with your work on the HR Assistant Onboarding Admin Checklist A4 from T5 and the tracking process from T7.

I have reviewed A3. The structure is solid and lines up with the touchpoints in A1. I suggested a few wording tweaks to make expectations clearer for managers, especially around buddy check-ins. Once those are in, I think A3 will be ready to approve under D5.

I started drafting the HR Assistant Onboarding Admin Checklist A4 for T5. It covers contracts, payroll setup, system access, and mandatory forms, but I am not fully sure how detailed the system access part should be. Should we list each system separately, or just refer to a central access request form?

For system access in A4, I recommend we keep it simple and refer to the central access request form, plus a short list of critical systems that must be requested for every new hire. That way the checklist stays manageable and we avoid constant updates when tools change.

On the tracking process for T7 and A5, I suggest we use a simple shared sheet with one row per new hire and columns for each mandatory module and key manager actions. HR assistants can own updating completion status, while managers confirm when their actions are done. We can then use this sheet to feed the metrics in T11.

I can maintain A5 if we keep it straightforward. My only concern is the time it might take to update every column for each new hire. Maybe we can limit the sheet to mandatory modules and the most important manager actions, and skip optional items so it stays realistic to manage.

Agree, A5 should only track mandatory modules and a few key manager actions. Optional items can be left out to avoid overcomplicating T7. I also support the idea that HR assistants own updating the sheet, with managers confirming their parts via a quick note or survey response.

From a training perspective, A5 as a simple sheet works well. We can also reference it in A6 so facilitators remind managers during the live sessions that completion is being tracked. That should help with adoption without adding heavy reporting.

I have incorporated your wording suggestions into A3 and clarified the buddy check-in expectations. With those changes, I believe the Manager Onboarding Toolkit and Checklist is ready. Unless there are objections, I propose we approve A3 under D5 as our standard manager toolkit for the pilot.

I have reviewed A4 for compliance. The sections on contracts, payroll, and mandatory forms look correct. I added one note about including the latest data privacy consent form. Once that is added, I am fine with A4 being used for the next intake.

I have updated A4 with the data privacy consent form and simplified the system access section as suggested. If there is anything else missing, let me know, but from my side the checklist now covers the main admin steps for each new hire.

To close T7, I suggest we document that HR assistants are the owners of updating A5, with managers responsible for confirming completion of their actions via the manager survey or a quick note. This gives us a clear owner and keeps the process light enough to sustain.

Agreed. Let us record that decision clearly: A5 will be our Onboarding Completion Tracking Sheet, focused on mandatory modules and key manager actions. HR assistants own updating the sheet, and managers confirm their actions. With that, we can consider the tracking process and owner defined under D6.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in communication plan, FAQ, and rollout timeline for pilot.

messages.text: I have shared a draft of the Onboarding Communication and FAQ Pack A8 for T9 and T10. It includes key messages for managers and new hires, announcement templates, and an initial FAQ list. The plan references the day 7 and day 30 surveys from A7 and the pilot flow from A1. Please review so we can finalize the communication plan and FAQ under D7 and then confirm the pilot cohort and dates under D8.

I reviewed A8. The messaging is clear and matches the structure in A1 and the live sessions in A2 and A6. I added a suggestion to highlight the two 45-minute live sessions so managers know exactly what to expect. For the FAQ, I think we should add one or two questions about how remote hires join in-person elements.

From a policy standpoint, the communication in A8 looks fine. I only flagged one item where we should avoid promising that all role-specific training is standardized, since some teams will still handle their own parts. Once that wording is adjusted, I am comfortable with the pack.

On A7 and the evaluation side, I drafted survey templates for new hires and managers at day 7 and day 30. The questions cover clarity, relevance, pacing, and overall satisfaction. In A8, I suggest we include one short line in the manager communication explaining that they will receive these surveys and that their feedback will shape future iterations.

I went through the FAQ section in A8. It already covers several common questions we hear, like pay dates and equipment. I can add a few more items from recent tickets, for example how to update personal details and where to find benefits information, so we reach at least 20 questions for T10.

Good call on setting expectations about the surveys. During the live sessions, I can also remind new hires that they will receive day 7 and day 30 surveys and that their feedback will help refine the program before we scale beyond the pilot.

I have updated A8 to clarify that core onboarding is standardized, while role-specific training remains with each team. I also incorporated the suggestions from 54023 and 173284 about highlighting the live session format and the surveys. With these edits, I believe the communication plan and FAQ pack are ready to approve under D7, unless anyone sees remaining gaps.

I have now expanded the FAQ in A8 with additional questions from recent cases, including how to change bank details and where to find the HR portal. If someone can quickly scan for consistency with A2 and A4, that would be helpful.
I checked the new FAQ entries in A8. They are consistent with our current HR processes and align with the information in A4. No changes needed from my side.
From the training side, the FAQ now lines up with what we present in A2 and A6, so new hires should not hear conflicting messages. Looks good to me.

On the pilot details for T12, I propose we use the next monthly intake as our pilot cohort, starting two weeks from Monday. That gives us enough time to finalize materials and brief managers. Evaluation checkpoints would be: 1) day 7 survey, 2) day 30 survey, and 3) a short internal debrief after the first cohort completes the 30 days. Does this timing work for everyone?

The proposed pilot start date works for me. I can run the two 45-minute live sessions for that cohort and make sure we capture informal feedback during and after the sessions to complement the surveys in A7.
From the HR assistant side, the timing is fine. I will make sure A4 and A5 are ready to use for that intake so we can test the admin checklist and tracking process during the pilot.

I am aligned with the proposed pilot cohort and checkpoints. After the first cohort completes the 30 days, I can help summarize survey results from A7 and lessons learned so we can prioritize improvements for the next round.

The timeline works for me as well. Just a note that we should inform senior leadership about the pilot dates and what we will measure, which is already outlined in A8 and T11. That will help manage expectations before we scale.

Given the feedback, let us confirm: 1) A8 is our approved communication and FAQ pack for managers and new hires under D7, and 2) the next monthly intake, starting two weeks from Monday, will be our pilot cohort with evaluation checkpoints at day 7, day 30, and a post-pilot debrief under D8. I will inform senior leadership and the relevant managers using the templates in A8.
